newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia will subsidise 1997 wheat price -paper.
newsitem.headline: Serbia will subsidise 1997 wheat price -paper.

text.p: Serbia's government will subsidise this year's wheat price with reference to the current market price, the Belgrade daily Politika said on Friday.
The Serbian government set the purchasing price of the 1997 wheat crop at 1.1 dinars per kilo, the paper said quoting republic's government statement.
Setting the price, the government wanted to protect the interests of agricultural producers in view of their contribution to economic and social stability, the statement said.

Serbia's purchasing price is by 0.1 dinars above the guaranteed 1997 wheat price set by the federal government which has fixed the wheat price at one dinar per kilo for the first class crop, 0.9 dinars for second and 0.8 for third class crop.

Yugoslavia, consisting of Serbia and Montenegro, has sown some 800,000 hectares under wheat this year, 217,000 ha up on the area sown the previous year. Out of this, 798,249 ha was sown in Serbia and 2,336 ha in Montenegro.
Serbia is expected to produce 2.749 million tonnes and Montenegro 6,059 tonnes of wheat this year.
Expected wheat production in Yugoslavia this year stands at 1.25 million tonnes above production in 1996. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 222 4254 ($1=5.7809)
